key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings can achieve dense, fine-lamellar microstructures with improved corrosion and wear performance when spray conditions promote well-flattened droplets and low porosity.
engineering_relevance: For protective coatings on carbon steel, optimizing spray parameters and operating humidity can materially affect long-term durability, making this relevant to corrosion-resistant surface engineering.
method: Detonation sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 carbon steel
Compared coating structures formed under different spraying parameters
Tested long-term corrosion and tribological behavior under different humidity conditions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that coatings with higher porosity showed reduced long-term corrosion resistance, while friction coefficient and wear rate decreased as humidity increased.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on process-induced porosity and environment, so results may not transfer directly without re-optimizing spray parameters and service humidity conditions.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
